List objects of a specific kind with filtering, sorting, pagination, grouping,
and optional field projection.



Full objects are loaded from storage (including overlays), then projection keeps
only the requested top-level keys,

reducing serialized output size. Use --fields with top-level YAML keys (repeat
flag or comma-separated values).

--sort-by and --group-by columns are included in the projection automatically
when those flags are set.



If no kind is specified, shows available object kinds.

  List all backlog items
  zqk list backlog_item
  List with filtering
  zqk list backlog_item --filter status=exploring
  List with sorting
  zqk list backlog_item --sort-by title --sort-asc
  List id and updated_at only (projection)
  zqk list backlog_item --fields id,updated_at --sort-by updated_at
  List with pagination
  zqk list backlog_item --offset 0 --limit 10
  List with grouping
  zqk list backlog_item --group-by status
  List with negation filter
  zqk list backlog_item --filter 'status!="complete|archived"'
  List with context-specific pagination (if configured)
  zqk list backlog_item --context pagination
  List with multiple filters
  zqk list backlog_item --filter status=exploring --filter priority=high
  Show available kinds
  zqk list

Usage:
  zqk object list [flags]

Aliases:
  list, ls, find

Flags:
      --allow-degraded       Allow running when scheduler daemon is not running (results may be partial/stale)
      --count                Only return the count of matching objects (no object details)
      --fields stringArray   Keys to include per object (repeat or comma-separated); omit for full rows. Sort/group columns merge automatically.
      --filter stringArray   Filter by field (format: field=value or field:value, can be used multiple times)
      --group-by string      Field to group results by
      --group-limit int      Maximum items per group when using --group-by (0 = no limit)
      --limit int            Pagination limit
      --offset int           Pagination offset
      --sort-asc             Sort ascending (default: true) (default true)
      --sort-by string       Field to sort by
